note: 30 candidates in this part. The session's shared web-search allowance was used up before this part began, Ballotpedia answered the kit's fetcher with an empty page, and louisvilleky.gov answered 403, so pages were read with the kit's own fetcher (states/net.py): county and city government sites, the Kentucky Court of Justice county pages, Wikipedia and Louisville Public Media. Campaign websites were found only by trying the candidate's own name as an address, and kept only where the site names the candidate and the office or place. Heavrin's site is the standing site of her State Representative committee (its home page still says she is running for re-election in 2024); it names her and the 18th District. Grossl's site names her and 'Fayette and Scott Counties' (House District 88's counties) but not the office. Heavrin and Grossl are sitting legislators with record pages, so only their websites and own words are recorded; their parties' candidate listings are already in ballot/lean/ky_endorsements.json. Parrish-Wright's Metro Council start year is left blank: Wikipedia's Louisville Metro Council table gives 2023 and its 2026 mayoral election article gives 2024. Nothing could be read for the constables (except Henry County's), magistrates, the Carroll sheriff, the Marion jailer, the Hardin PVA, the district judge (the Calloway and Marshall court pages list no Chris Hendricks), the Elizabethtown, Hopkinsville and Richmond candidates (none is listed on the city's own council page) or the three school-board candidates, so they are left out.
